text:
The Kings arrive on the second night of a back-to-back stretch of short rest, riding an overtime win at NYI on Oct. 22 in which Brandt Clarke scored the winner and Darcy Kuemper made 41 saves. They are 2-2-1 in their last five and still without Quinton Byfield and Alex Turcotte. The Devils beat ANA 4-1 that same night and are 4-1-0 in their last five, outscoring teams 22-13.

The story here is a team that is better than its results against one trying to climb out. NJD has taken 60% of the five-on-five expected goals (a measure of chance quality), while LAK sits at 50% and takes 4.6 penalties a game. Both teams have been hurt by finishing and goaltending. The projected starters, Anton Forsberg and Jake Allen, are both well below expected this season, at -2.1 and -3.4 goals saved above expected, though each was in the black last year. Our model projects 3.16 goals for NJD and 2.73 for LAK.

Watch Jack Hughes, our model's top pick on either side at 35% to score. Nico Hischier, a power-play threat, is right behind at 31%. For LAK, Adrian Kempe leads at 35%. With Byfield out, Alex Laferriere has moved onto a line with Panarin and Kempe and is up to 22:17 a night from 18:44. Artemi Panarin, signed as a free agent after the KHL, is the Kings' best bet for multiple points.
